comment: IEEE 802.11b DSSS with the long PLCP: SYNC, SFD and the PLCP header at 1 Mb/s DBPSK, then the PSDU at the rate the header's SIGNAL field gives (1 or 2 Mb/s DQPSK), switched mid-packet. Barker-11 at 11 Mchip/s (timing and carrier estimated on the chips, the carrier by the 4th power: every chip is on an axis), self-synchronizing scrambler, RRC 0.35 for the spectral mask. Receiving, the header is read after the demapper has demapped the PSDU at the old rate, so the runner re-runs that span from its buffer; transmitting, SIGNAL comes from the caller's fields, else the `signal` parameter

signal.comment: transmit: the PSDU rate in 100 kb/s, 10 or 20, unless the caller gives one per packet
